name: Augustine of Hippo
credit: Saint Augustine by Philippe de Champaigne, c. 1645–50 · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Augustine was born in 354 at Thagaste in Roman North Africa. He trained as a rhetorician and taught the subject at Carthage, Rome and Milan.

He was converted to Christianity in 386 and baptised the following year. He returned to Africa, was ordained priest at Hippo, and from 395 or 396 served as its bishop until his death in 430, as the Vandals besieged the city.

He wrote the Confessions and The City of God, and many sermons and letters. The letters in this selection, translated by James Houston Baxter for the Loeb Classical Library, range from his early philosophical correspondence to the pastoral and controversial writing of his years as bishop.
